full_text_en:
Jianhu County People's Procuratorate, Jiangsu Province v. Zhang Shaoshan et al. (32 persons)  

— Criminal and Ancillary Civil Public Interest Litigation for Illegal Mining and for Ma Chaoyu's Concealment of Criminal Proceeds

**Case Abstract**

In the crime of illegal sand mining, where the sand miner and the sand purchaser collude in advance and engage in illegal sand mining through an integrated mining-and-transportation method, forming a production-sales chain of profit, the sand purchaser shall be found to have formed a joint crime of illegal sand mining with the sand miner.

In determining the ecological and environmental damage caused by illegal sand mining, the assessment shall be comprehensive, based on quantitative indicators such as the volume of sand mined, the direct loss of fish resources, the number of benthic organisms harmed, and the value of ecosystem service losses.

For a defendant who has a prior criminal record of illegal sand mining or who again commits illegal sand mining while released on bail pending trial for illegal sand mining, the defendant shall be found to have the intent to damage the ecological environment. Where the procuratorial authority requests the defendant to bear punitive damages, the people's court shall support such request.

**Prosecutor and Ancillary Civil Public Interest Litigation Plaintiff:** Jianhu County People's Procuratorate, Jiangsu Province.

**Defendants and Defendants in the Ancillary Civil Action:** Zhang Shaoshan, Zhang Jinchen, Ding Chao, Cheng Chao, Hong Ziwu, Wang Qianhong, Li Yong, Zhang Hengwei, Feng Taiping, Ling Jinhua, Bao Awen, Zhang Yugao, Wang Yuanjing, Shang Xuelu (hereinafter referred to as "Zhang Shaoshan et al. (14 persons)").

**Defendants:** Guan Shaoyun, Ke Shengfu, Shen Wei, Cheng Rui, Song Jie, Fang Chen, Fang Yunfeng, Fang Qiutong, He Ming, Xiao Han, Xiao Shangbin, Cheng Quanfu, He Heyou, He Shenghua, Liu Yang, Lyu Yuming, Ling Laishui, Ling Yun, Ma Chaoyu.

Jianhu County People's Procuratorate, Jiangsu Province, indicted the defendants and defendants in the ancillary civil action—Zhang Shaoshan, Zhang Jinchen, Ding Chao, Cheng Chao, Hong Ziwu, Wang Qianhong, Li Yong, Zhang Hengwei, Feng Taiping, Ling Jinhua, Bao Awen, Zhang Yugao, Wang Yuanjing, Shang Xuelu, and the defendants Guan Shaoyun, Ke Shengfu, Shen Wei, Cheng Rui, Song Jie, Fang Chen, Fang Yunfeng, Fang Qiutong, He Ming, Xiao Han, Xiao Shangbin, Cheng Quanfu, He Heyou, He Shenghua, Liu Yang, Lyu Yuming, Ling Laishui, Ling Yun (hereinafter referred to as "Zhang Shaoshan et al. (32 persons)") for the crime of illegal mining, and the defendant Ma Chaoyu for the crime of concealing criminal proceeds, and filed the indictment with the Dongtai City People's Court, Jiangsu Province, while also initiating an ancillary civil public interest lawsuit.

The Jianhu County People's Procuratorate, Jiangsu Province, alleged the following:

(1) Around March and April 2021, the defendant Li Yong and others plotted to illegally mine sand. They contacted the defendant Wang Qianhong, the owner of a sand mining vessel, and agreed that Li Yong's side would provide a deposit of RMB 700,000 and Wang Qianhong would provide the "three-no" sand mining vessel "Wan Mingxin 26", each holding a 50% share, to jointly engage in illegal sand mining, with profits to be split equally. From April 13 to April 19, 2021, the defendants Wang Qianhong, Li Yong, Cheng Chao, Fang Chen, Fang Yunfeng, Fang Qiutong, Xiao Han, Xiao Shangbin, Liu Yang, and others, together with Hu Caifan, Chen Jiawei, and Xu Yang (all separately prosecuted), using the "Wan Mingxin 26" and other "three-no" sand mining vessels, and the defendant Shang Xuelu and others, owners of sand transport vessels, engaged in illegal sand mining in the prohibited mining area on the river surface opposite the No. 8 red buoy of Donggang, Tongling section of the Yangtze River, upstream of Laozhoutou Ferry, on the side near Jiangxinzhou, using a method of collusion in advance and integrated mining and transportation.

(2) In June 2021, the defendants Zhang Shaoshan, Ding Chao, Zhang Jinchen, Cheng Chao, Guan Shaoyun, and Ke Shengfu provided a deposit of over RMB 1 million for a 50% share, and the defendants Hong Ziwu and others provided the "three-no" sand mining vessel "Wan Qinhua 966" for a 50% share; both sides agreed to split profits equally for joint illegal sand mining. Later, Zhang Shaoshan, Zhang Jinchen, Ding Chao, Cheng Chao, and Hong Ziwu assembled the defendants Guan Shaoyun, Ke Shengfu, Shen Wei, Cheng Rui, Song Jie, He Ming, Xiao Han, Xiao Shangbin, and Chen Jiawei, along with the transport vessel side defendants Zhang Hengwei, Lyu Yuming, and Feng Taiping, and engaged in illegal sand mining while clearly knowing that they had not obtained a river sand mining permit.

(3) At the end of June 2021, Hong Ziwu and others sold the "three-no" sand mining vessel "Wan Qinhua 966" to Zhang Shaoshan, Zhang Jinchen, and Ding Chao. Zhang Shaoshan, Zhang Jinchen, and Ding Chao assembled the defendants Shen Wei, Cheng Rui, Song Jie, Xiao Shangbin, Cheng Quanfu, He Heyou, He Shenghua, and others, and together with the transport vessel side defendants Ling Jinhua, Ling Laishui, Ling Yun, Wang Yuanjing, Bao Awen, and Zhang Yugao, engaged in illegal sand mining while clearly knowing that they had not obtained a river sand mining permit.

(4) On the night of March 12 and the early morning of March 13, 2021, the defendant Bao Awen conspired with others to illegally mine sand in the prohibited mining area on the river surface between the No. 5 and No. 6 red buoys of Donggang, Tongling section of the Yangtze River.

(5) On the night of July 7 and the early morning of July 8, 2021, the defendant Ma Chaoyu, knowing that the river sand on Ling Jinhua's sand transport vessel "Wan Shouxian 816" was illegally mined, purchased at least 1,700 tons at RMB 90 per ton, of which more than 1,000 tons were sold to a small sand transport vessel at RMB 94 per ton, yielding RMB 95,000; the remaining river sand was loaded onto another small vessel, and the sand purchase price had not yet been collected.

The procuratorial authority submitted that Zhang Shaoshan et al. (32 persons), during the prohibited sand mining period in the main stream of the Yangtze River below Yibin, engaged in illegal sand mining through a model of prior collusion and integrated mining and transportation, constituting the crime of illegal mining; Ma Chaoyu, knowing that the river sand on Ling Jinhua's transport vessel was illegally mined, agreed to purchase it, constituting the crime of concealing criminal proceeds; and accordingly, Zhang Shaoshan et al. (32 persons) and Ma Chaoyu should be punished in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Criminal Law.

The ancillary civil public interest litigation plaintiff alleged that the facts were substantially consistent with the criminal allegations. In addition, a technical assessment report prepared by the Forensic Appraisal Institute of Nanjing University Environmental Planning and Design Institute Group Co., Ltd. found that the illegal sand mining activities of the defendants Zhang Shaoshan et al. (14 persons) caused ecological and environmental damage at the incident site, and that there was a causal relationship between the sand mining activities of Zhang Shaoshan et al. (14 persons) and the ecological and environmental damage. The estimated volume of river sand resource loss due to illegal sand mining was 23,382.52 cubic meters, and the assessed amount of ecological and environmental damage to the Yangtze River was RMB 5,157,476.86. Zhang Shaoshan et al. (14 persons), without obtaining a river sand mining permit, illegally mined sand in the prohibited mining period and area in the Tongling section of the Yangtze River and other sections, thereby damaging the mineral resources and ecological environment of the waters involved and harming the public interest; they should bear tort liability. The defendant Zhang Shaoshan had previously been criminally punished for the crime of illegal mining, and the defendant Bao Awen again committed illegal sand mining while released on bail pending trial for suspected illegal mining; they should bear punitive damages liability. Therefore, the plaintiff requested: (1) an order that Zhang Shaoshan et al. (14 persons) bear joint and several liability for the assessed ecological and environmental damage of RMB 5,157,476.86 within the scope of their respective volumes of sand mining participation; (2) an order that Zhang Shaoshan et al. (14 persons) bear joint and several liability for the assessment costs of RMB 280,000; (3) an order that Zhang Shaoshan and Bao Awen each bear punitive damages of one times the ecological and environmental damage caused by their respective participation; and (4) an order that Zhang Shaoshan et al. (14 persons) publicly apologize to the public in national media.

All defendants had no objection to the criminal facts and charges alleged by the procuratorial authority and pleaded guilty and accepted punishment in court.

The defendant Bao Awen argued that the location of his sand mining on March 12–13, 2021, was not a prohibited mining area, and that after being arrested, he truthfully confessed the criminal facts. The defendant Xiao Han also argued that after being brought to justice, he truthfully confessed the criminal facts.

The defendants in the ancillary civil action, Zhang Shaoshan, Hong Ziwu, Wang Qianhong, Li Yong, Feng Taiping, Ling Jinhua, Zhang Yugao, Wang Yuanjing, and Shang Xuelu, had no objection to the claims of the public interest litigation plaintiff and expressed willingness to compensate. The defendants in the ancillary civil action, Zhang Jinchen, Ding Chao, Cheng Chao, Zhang Hengwei, and Bao Awen, argued that they should not bear joint and several liability, but also expressed willingness to compensate.

The defense counsel for the defendants Zhang Shaoshan, Hong Ziwu, Wang Qianhong, Zhang Yugao, Wang Yuanjing, Guan Shaoyun, Ke Shengfu, Fang Yunfeng, and Cheng Quanfu primarily argued that the respective defendants had mitigating circumstances such as being accessories, truthful confessions, meritorious service, guilty pleas and acceptance of punishment, and restitution of illegal gains, and requested lenient punishment.

The defense counsel for the defendants Zhang Jinchen, Ding Chao, and Cheng Chao primarily argued that the respective defendants should be found to be accessories in the joint crime and had mitigating circumstances such as voluntary surrender, truthful confessions, guilty pleas and acceptance of punishment, and restitution of illegal gains, and requested lenient punishment.

The defense counsel for the defendants Li Yong, Feng Taiping, and Ling Jinhua primarily argued that the respective defendants played a minor role in the joint crime and had mitigating circumstances such as truthful confessions, guilty pleas and acceptance of punishment, and restitution of illegal gains, and requested lenient punishment.

The defense counsel for the defendant Shang Xuelu primarily argued that Shang Xuelu subjectively intended to purchase sand, not to mine sand, and therefore did not constitute the crime of illegal mining but should constitute the crime of concealing criminal proceeds.

The defense counsel for the defendants Fang Qiutong and Liu Yang primarily argued that Shang Xuelu's profit from resale at a markup should not be included in the value of the illegal sand mining participated in by these two defendants, and that they had mitigating circumstances such as guilty pleas and acceptance of punishment and restitution of illegal gains, and requested lenient punishment.

The Dongtai City People's Court, Jiangsu Province, found through trial the following facts:

On the night of March 12, 2021, to the early morning of March 13, 2021, the defendant Bao Awen, using the sand transport vessel "Honghe 568", together with a sand mining vessel contacted in advance, jointly illegally mined 3,069.84 tons of sand in the prohibited mining area on the river surface between the No. 5 and No. 6 red buoys of Donggang, Tongling section of the Yangtze River, using the integrated mining-and-transportation method. The sand was later seized by the public security authorities while in transit for sale. The assessed value of the river sand was RMB 202,609.

In March and April 2021, the defendant Li Yong and others contacted the defendant Wang Qianhong through an intermediary, and agreed that Li Yong's side would provide a deposit of RMB 1.1 million (RMB 700,000 actually paid) and Wang Qianhong would provide the "three-no" sand mining vessel "Wan Mingxin 26" for joint illegal sand mining, with profits to be split equally. From April 13 to April 19, 2021, the defendants Li Yong, Cheng Chao, Fang Yunfeng, Fang Chen, Fang Qiutong, Liu Yang, Xiao Han, Xiao Shangbin, and Chen Jiawei and Xu Yang (both separately prosecuted), using Wang Qianhong's "Wan Mingxin 26" and other sand mining vessels, together with the pre-contacted transport vessel owner defendant Shang Xuelu and others, engaged in illegal sand mining four times in the prohibited mining area on the river surface opposite the No. 8 red buoy of Donggang, Tongling section of the Yangtze River, upstream of Laozhoutou Ferry, on the side near Jiangxinzhou, using the integrated mining-and-transportation method, totaling 13,900 tons, valued at RMB 476,900.

In June 2021, the defendants Zhang Shaoshan, Ding Chao, Zhang Jinchen, and Cheng Chao provided a deposit of RMB 1.3 million (over RMB 1 million actually paid) for a 50% share, and the defendants Hong Ziwu and others provided the "three-no" sand mining vessel originally registered as "Wan Jinrui 666" and later renamed "Wan Qinhua 966" for a 50% share, for joint illegal sand mining, with profits to be split equally. Later, Cheng Chao recruited the defendants Guan Shaoyun and Ke Shengfu to invest and participate in the sand mining. On the night of June 22 to the early morning of June 24, 2021, Zhang Shaoshan, Ding Chao, Zhang Jinchen, and Cheng Chao assembled the defendants Guan Shaoyun, Ke Shengfu, Shen Wei, Cheng Rui, Song Jie, He Ming, Xiao Han, Xiao Shangbin, and Chen Jiawei, and without obtaining a sand mining permit, using Hong Ziwu's "Wan Qinhua 966" sand mining vessel, together with the pre-contacted transport vessel side defendants Zhang Hengwei and Feng Taiping, engaged in illegal sand mining twice in the prohibited mining area on the river surface opposite the No. 8 red buoy of Donggang, Tongling section of the Yangtze River, downstream of Laozhoutou Ferry, on the side near Jiangxinzhou, using the integrated mining-and-transportation method, totaling 5,180 tons, valued at RMB 485,000.

At the end of June 2021, the defendants Hong Ziwu and others sold the "three-no" sand mining vessel "Wan Qinhua 966" to the defendants Zhang Shaoshan, Zhang Jinchen, and Ding Chao. Zhang Shaoshan held a 60% share, Zhang Jinchen held a 20% share, and Ding Chao held a 20% share; after deducting 45% of the income as a commission for Zhang Shaoshan, the remaining was distributed according to their shareholding ratios. On the night of July 6 to the early morning of July 9, 2021, Zhang Shaoshan, Zhang Jinchen, and Ding Chao assembled the defendants Shen Wei, Cheng Rui, Song Jie, Xiao Shangbin, Cheng Quanfu, He Heyou, He Shenghua, and others, and without obtaining a sand mining permit, together with the pre-contacted transport vessel side defendants Ling Jinhua, Wang Yuanjing, Bao Awen, and Zhang Yugao, engaged in illegal sand mining three times in the waters near the No. 253 white buoy of the Yangtze River, using the integrated mining-and-transportation method, totaling 24,615.2 tons, valued at RMB 1,728,620.

On the night of July 7 to the early morning of July 8, 2021, the defendants Ling Jinhua, Ling Laishui, Ling Yun, and others illegally mined sand in the waters near the No. 253 white buoy of the Yangtze River, of which the sand transport vessel "Wan Shouxian 816" measured approximately 2,900 tons of sand mined. The defendant Ma Chaoyu, knowing that the river sand on the vessel "Wan Shouxian 816" was illegally mined, purchased at least 1,700 tons at RMB 90 per ton, and sold more than 1,000 tons to a small sand transport vessel at RMB 94 per ton, yielding RMB 95,000; the remaining river sand was loaded onto another small sand transport vessel, and the sand purchase price had not yet been collected. Ma Chaoyu illegally profited RMB 1,500, which has been surrendered.

After the case was discovered, the defendant Zhang Shaoshan surrendered illegal gains of RMB 178,600; the defendant Zhang Jinchen surrendered illegal gains of RMB 78,275; the defendant Ding Chao surrendered illegal gains of RMB 90,000; the defendant Fang Yunfeng surrendered illegal gains of RMB 1,400; the defendant Liu Yang surrendered illegal gains of RMB 1,600; the defendants Ke Shengfu, Feng Taiping, Shang Xuelu, Shen Wei, Cheng Rui, He Ming, Fang Chen, Fang Qiutong, Xiao Han, and Xiao Shangbin surrendered all illegal gains.

The 3,069.84 tons of river sand lawfully seized by the public security authorities from the defendant Bao Awen were sold for RMB 202,609; the 2,555 tons of river sand lawfully seized from the defendant Ling Jinhua were sold for RMB 166,928; the 2,623.9 tons of river sand lawfully seized from the defendant Wang Yuanjing were sold for RMB 181,915; the 2,791.3 tons of river sand lawfully seized from the defendants Zhang Yugao and Bao Awen were sold for RMB 183,305.

The defendants Ding Chao and Lyu Yuming voluntarily surrendered and truthfully confessed the criminal facts. The defendants Hong Ziwu, Ling Jinhua, Ling Yun, Ling Laishui, and Shen Wei truthfully confessed their crimes after being brought to justice.

It was further found that the prohibited sand mining period in the main stream of the Yangtze River below Yibin is from June 1 to September 30 each year. The river sections in the freshwater dolphin national nature reserve in the Tongling section of the Yangtze River in Anhui Province, including the branch river where the Donggang waterway of the Tongling section is located and the river area of the No. 253 white buoy of the Yangtze River, are all prohibited mining areas for river sand. Since January 2020, no sand mining permits have been issued in the Anhui section of the Yangtze River.

The Forensic Appraisal Institute of Nanjing University Environmental Planning and Design Institute Group Co., Ltd. prepared a technical assessment report. The report found that the illegal sand mining activities of the defendants Zhang Shaoshan and others caused ecological and environmental damage at the incident site, and that there was a causal relationship between the activities and the ecological and environmental damage to the Yangtze River. The assessed amount of ecological and environmental damage to the Yangtze River was RMB 5,157,476.86, including RMB 4,910,329.2 for damage to riverbed structure, RMB 96,146.02 for damage to fish resources, RMB 14,884.62 for damage to benthic organisms, RMB 101,557.02 for loss of biodiversity service value, and RMB 34,560 for subsequent monitoring costs. The report recommended that compensation for riverbed structure damage be made in an amount equivalent to the resource value, and that compensation for aquatic organism damage be made in an amount equivalent to the value of stock enhancement and release. The assessment costs for this case were RMB 280,000.

The Dongtai City People's Court, Jiangsu Province, held in its judgment:

The Yangtze River, as China's life river and mother river, is an important support for the development of the Chinese nation. River sand in the Yangtze River channel is a national mineral resource, and illegal mining of river sand will damage the ecological environment of the Yangtze River and affect the stability of the river regime, flood control, and navigation safety.

**I. The defendants Zhang Shaoshan et al. (32 persons) constituted the crime of illegal mining and were joint offenders.**

Article 28 of the Yangtze River Protection Law of the PRC provides that the state establishes a planning and licensing system for sand mining in the Yangtze River basin. Sand mining in the Yangtze River basin shall be licensed by the relevant river basin management agency of the water administrative department of the State Council or by the water administrative department of the people's government at or above the county level. The relevant river basin management agency of the water administrative department of the State Council and the people's governments at or above the county level in the Yangtze River basin shall, in accordance with the law, designate prohibited sand mining areas and prohibited sand mining periods, and strictly control the sand mining areas, total sand mining volumes, and the number of sand mining vessels within sand mining areas. It is prohibited to engage in sand mining activities in prohibited sand mining areas and during prohibited sand mining periods in the Yangtze River basin. Article 9 of the Regulations on the Administration of Sand Mining in the Yangtze River Channel provides that the state implements a sand mining licensing system for sand mining in the Yangtze River.

1. In this case, the defendants Zhang Shaoshan et al. (32 persons), without obtaining a river sand mining permit, engaged in illegal sand mining in the prohibited mining period and prohibited mining area of the Yangtze River, and all constituted the crime of illegal mining. The defendant Ma Chaoyu, knowing that the purchased river sand was proceeds of crime of others, purchased it, and his conduct constituted the crime of concealing criminal proceeds. The criminal facts alleged by the procuratorial authority were clear, the evidence was reliable and sufficient, and the charges were established; the court supported them.

2. This case was a joint intentional crime. The defendants Zhang Shaoshan, Zhang Jinchen, Ding Chao, Cheng Chao, Hong Ziwu, Wang Qianhong, Li Yong, Zhang Hengwei, Feng Taiping, Ling Jinhua, Wang Yuanjing, Bao Awen, Zhang Yugao, and Shang Xuelu were shareholders, sand mining vessel owners, or pre-colluding sand purchasers who played a principal role in the joint crime; they were principal offenders and should be punished in accordance with all crimes in which they participated. The defendants Guan Shaoyun, Ke Shengfu, Shen Wei, Cheng Rui, Song Jie, Fang Chen, Fang Qiutong, Fang Yunfeng, He Ming, Cheng Quanfu, He Heyou, He Shenghua, Xiao Han, Xiao Shangbin, Liu Yang, Lyu Yuming, Ling Yun, and Ling Laishui were engaged in tasks such as standing guard, measuring volume, contacting and introducing sand purchasers, collecting sand money, mining sand, and releasing sand; they played a secondary role in the joint crime and were accessories, and were given a lighter or mitigated punishment in accordance with the law.

3. The court considered circumstances such as recidivism, voluntary surrender, truthful confession, and meritorious service respectively. The defendants Fang Chen and Xiao Han had previously been sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment or heavier punishment for intentional crimes, and within five years after the completion of the execution of the punishment, they again committed crimes punishable by fixed-term imprisonment or heavier punishment; they were recidivists and were given a heavier punishment in accordance with the law. The defendants Ding Chao and Lyu Yuming voluntarily surrendered and truthfully confessed the criminal facts; they had voluntary surrender and were given a lighter punishment in accordance with the law. The defendants Hong Ziwu, Ling Jinhua, Shen Wei, Ling Yun, and Ling Laishui truthfully confessed their crimes after being brought to justice; they were given a lighter punishment in accordance with the law. The defendants Zhang Shaoshan, Hong Ziwu, and Fang Qiutong provided leads to crimes committed by others, which had not yet been verified; the defendants Wang Yuanjing and Ke Shengfu persuaded and accompanied co-defendants to turn themselves in; they had meritorious service and were given a lighter punishment in accordance with the law. All defendants voluntarily pleaded guilty and accepted punishment, and were given a lenient punishment in accordance with the law.

**II. The defendants Zhang Shaoshan et al. (14 persons) should bear civil tort liability.**

Illegal sand mining activities not only cause damage to national resource assets but also harm the ecological environment, resulting in damage to national interests and the social public interest. Mineral resources have both economic and ecological attributes. It is not permissible to focus only on protecting the economic value of mineral resources while neglecting relief for the ecological value of mineral resources. Therefore, in accordance with the principle of "who pollutes, who governs; who destroys, who bears responsibility," the liability for ecological damage compensation of persons engaged in illegal sand mining shall be pursued in accordance with the law.

1. This case constitutes a major illegal mining case in which lawbreakers brazenly committed crimes after the implementation of the Yangtze River Protection Law of the PRC. Notably, the sand mining site is located between the upper and lower cross-sections of the Tongling Freshwater Dolphin National Nature Reserve in Anhui Province. This area is rich in planktonic plants, planktonic animals, and benthic organisms, including dozens of fish species, as well as aquatic wild protected animals such as Chinese sturgeons and finless porpoises. The defendants Zhang Shaoshan and others illegally mined 46,765.04 tons of sand, an enormous quantity. This not only caused significant loss to the river sand resources of the Yangtze River, but also disrupted the balance between river sediment and water flow transport capacity within the mining area, leading to river regime instability and water level decline, directly threatening the safety of flood control, navigation, and other aspects of the Yangtze River. More seriously, this illegal sand mining directly caused damage to the ecosystem of the Yangtze River waters where the incident occurred, destroyed the breeding and living environment for aquatic animal resources, and adversely affected the richness and diversity of aquatic plants and animals in the Yangtze River.

2. Article 1229 of the Civil Code of the PRC provides that where any damage is caused to another person due to environmental pollution or ecological destruction, the tortfeasor shall bear tort liability. Article 1168 of the same Code provides that where two or more persons jointly commit a tort causing damage to another person, they shall be jointly and severally liable. Based on the facts found through trial and in accordance with the above legal provisions, the defendants Zhang Shaoshan and the other 13 persons constituted joint tortfeasors within the scope of their respective participation in illegal sand mining and shall bear joint and several civil liability for compensation for the ecological damage to the Yangtze River within the scope of their respective participation in the illegal sand mining. In this case, the judicial appraisal institution conducted a comprehensive appraisal of the damage caused by the illegal sand mining activities of Zhang Shaoshan and others to river sand resources, riverbed structure, water environment quality, and aquatic biological resources. Based on indicators such as the quantity of sand mined, direct loss of fish resources, number of damaged benthic organisms, and the value of ecosystem service, it quantified various types of damage costs including damage to the riverbed, damage to fish resources, damage to benthic biological resources, and damage to ecological service functions. This appraisal report is scientific, comprehensive, and reasonable. As none of the defendants in the incidental civil public interest litigation submitted rebuttal evidence to overturn the appraisal report, all damage costs and appraisal fees stated in the appraisal report are confirmed.

3. Paragraph 2 of Article 20 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Environmental Civil Public Interest Litigation provides that, while ordering the defendant to restore the ecological environment, the people's court may also determine the fees for ecological environment restoration which the defendant shall bear if it fails to perform the restoration obligation; or it may directly order the defendant to bear the fees for ecological environment restoration. As the defendants Zhang Shaoshan and the other 13 persons are ordinary natural persons, it is not feasible for them to directly restore the damaged Yangtze River ecological environment and fishery resources. Therefore, they may be ordered to bear the costs for restoration of ecological environment damage.

4. The defendant in the incidental civil public interest litigation, Zhang Shaoshan, had previously been sentenced to criminal punishment for the crime of illegal mining. The defendant Bao Awen committed the crime of illegal mining again while released on bail pending trial for suspected illegal mining. It can be determined that these two defendants had subjective malice in damaging the Yangtze River's ecological environment, with serious consequences. Pursuant to Article 1232 of the Civil Code of the PRC, they shall bear liability for punitive damages. In this case, a total of 46,765.04 tons of sand were illegally mined, of which Zhang Shaoshan participated in mining 29,795.2 tons and Bao Awen participated in mining 2,791.3 tons. The value of the ecological damage other than the loss of river sand resources in this case is RMB 212,587.66. Therefore, the public interest litigator's request that the two defendants bear punitive damages of one times the amount, i.e., RMB 135,445.02 and RMB 12,688.88 respectively, in proportion to the quantity of illegal sand mined, has factual and legal basis, and is supported by the people's court.

Based on the facts, nature, circumstances, and degree of harm to society of the crimes in this case, and taking into account the specific criminal circumstances and the defendants' expressions of guilt and remorse, the Dongtai People's Court of Jiangsu Province, in accordance with Article 343, Paragraph 1, Article 312, Paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law of the PRC, Articles 179 and 1232 of the Civil Code of the PRC, Article 93 of the Yangtze River Protection Law of the PRC, Articles 15 and 101, Paragraph 2 of the Criminal Procedure Law of the PRC, and Article 20 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Cases of Procuratorial Public Interest Litigation, rendered the following criminal附带 civil judgment on March 1, 2022: The 32 defendants including Zhang Shaoshan were respectively sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment ranging from one year to four years and six months, and fines ranging from RMB 15,000 to RMB 200,000 for the crime of illegal mining; the defendant Ma Zhaoyu was sentenced to one year and six months' fixed-term imprisonment, suspended for two years, and a fine of RMB 20,000 for the crime of concealing and disguising criminal proceeds; the defendants Zhang Shaoshan and the other 13 persons were ordered to bear joint and several liability for compensation for the ecological environment damage to the Yangtze River caused by their illegal sand mining activities in the amount of RMB 5,157,476.86, according to their respective participation in the criminal acts, and to publicly apologize on a national media platform; and Zhang Shaoshan and Bao Awen were ordered to bear punitive damages of one times the amount, i.e., RMB 135,445.02 and RMB 12,688.88 respectively, for the ecological environment damage to the Yangtze River caused by their participation in the illegal sand mining.

After the judgment of first instance was pronounced, none of the defendants appealed and the procuratorial authority did not lodge a protest. The judgment of first instance has become legally effective.
